summary: All obligations remain disposed with no pending work and audit-unit capacity exhausted, so this step continues the authorized source work on the deferred transport surface by reading the TCP stream layer, the stream-context lifecycle and the in-process peer registration. Submission is a feedback-only research product (no map version). Answered: newTCPTransport binds with net.Listen("tcp", bindAddr), wraps the listener in TCPStreamLayer with an optional advertise address, rejects a non-TCP listener address (errNotTCP) or an unspecified/absent advertise address (errNotAdvertisable) before creating the transport through a creator callback, and Dial/Accept/Close/Addr are plain delegation with Addr preferring the advertised address (tcp_transport.go 23-117); setupStreamContext creates a cancellable context, getStreamContext reads it under its lock, and CloseStreams releases every pooled connection then cancels and recreates the context under both the pool and context locks, with the code's own comment that the ordering prevents handlers holding a never-cancellable context (net_transport.go 285-331), while Close closes shutdownCh and the stream layer once (333-345); in-process Connect/Disconnect/DisconnectAll mutate the peers map under the transport lock and Disconnect also closes and compacts pipelines for that peer (inmem_transport.go 215-250). The feedback also corrects an item I had listed in the previous step without having read it: there is no TLS code in the captured library (no NetworkTransportConfig.TLSConfig and no tls use outside tests), so TLS can only come from a caller-supplied StreamLayer, and that item is explicitly withdrawn rather than left as an unread library responsibility. Remaining list keeps the surface deferred only on two narrow unread details - the in-process peer consumer-channel capacity and whether an address-provider change can race an in-flight dial - plus the un-re-checked heartbeat classification, the note that caller-supplied StreamLayer wrappers are outside the library, and the previously recorded open items (installSnapshot reachability, the compacted-leader variant, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences). Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
